svg.text: Explain It Like You Built It: The Viewport Physics of Streaming Auto-Scroll
How a Single DOM Subtraction Formula Eliminates Streaming Viewport Jitter in React 19
THE RECEIPT PAPER ROLL (DOM Scroll Geometry)
scrollHeight
The total paper roll length.
Grows +20px with every streamed token.
scrollTop
How far rolled up off the top screen edge.
clientHeight (Your Screen Window)
Fixed height window (e.g. 800px laptop screen).
distance = (scrollHeight - scrollTop - clientHeight)
If distance <= 60px: Pinned to Bottom (Auto-Follow)
If distance > 60px: Leash Snapped (Release User Scroll)
NAIVE STREAMING AUTO-SCROLL (The "Stupid Bot")
useEffect(() => { el.scrollIntoView() }, [streamToken]);
• Fires 30-50 times per second during high-speed LLM generation.
• Violently hijacks the mouse wheel when user scrolls up to read.
• Frustrates users trying to copy code snippets or re-read instructions.
[Result: Jarring layout shift & broken human reading experience]
SMART 60px LEASH PHYSICS (Our Implementation)
const atBottom = (scrollHeight - scrollTop - clientHeight) <= 60;
• When reading at the bottom: Auto-scrolls smoothly with incoming tokens.
• When scrolling up: Snaps leash at 61px; auto-scroll instantly turns off.
• Floating Beacon: Displays "↓ New tokens below" button with live counter.
[Result: Seamless reading control, zero fighting with the browser]
WHAT THIS PROVES: STAYING THE HUMAN IN THE LOOP

AI can spit out boilerplate scroll hooks in three seconds. But understanding DOM reflow costs, writing defensive fallbacks for JSDOM in automated tests, and engineering human reading ergonomics separates copy-paste code from production engineering.
